newsitem.title: JORDAN: Chirac says Iraq suffering "unworthy of modern age".
newsitem.headline: Chirac says Iraq suffering "unworthy of modern age".

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac, warning of a humanitarian disaster, appealed to the international community on Thursday to make good on an agreement to allow Iraq to sell limited amounts of oil to buy food.

Chirac told a joint news conference in Amman with Jordan's King Hussein that the situation in Iraq, which faces widespread malnutrition and infant mortality due to a six-year U.N. trade embargo, was "unworthy of the modern age".

"The population is suffering more and more and the health situation is disturbing," Chirac said. "This is unacceptable from a humanitarian point of view and extremely dangerous from a political point of view to the stability of the region."

Earlier on Thursday Chirac used a speech to Jordan's parliament to highlight his differences with the United States over Iraq, which has been under stringent trade sanctions since its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"France is alarmed at the humanitarian situation in Iraq and calls solemnly on the international community to apply at long last Resolution 986, which provides for the resumption of oil exports against the purchase of food and medicine to save innocent lives from tragedy," he said.

In a clear reference to Washington, which is holding up a deal agreed last May to implement the resolution, Chirac said: "The Iraqi people cannot be held responsible for decisions to which it was not party, nor can it be held hostage for stakes that are alien to it.
"The way ahead is clear, and involves the implementation of all Security Council resolutions -- but only those resolutions," he said to thunderous applause.

French officials privately accuse the United States of thwarting any easing of the stranglehold on Iraq by adding demands on President Saddam Hussein that go beyond U.N. resolutions calling for Iraq's partial disarmament, recognition of Kuwait and compensation for Gulf War damage.
Chirac said later at the news conference that "obstacles from both sides" were blocking implementation of the deal.

King Hussein, who has called for the overthrow of Saddam and provided a haven for the Iraqi opposition, said he shared Chirac's concern and hoped there would be an opportunity for "inter-Iraqi dialogue to resolve all problems".
"A healthy Iraq in this region is a necessity," he said.

In September, Washington blocked implementation of the oil-for-food deal following a renewed confrontation with Baghdad over Iraq's intervention in fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq.
In New York, U.N. diplomats said it could take months to put Resolution 986 into practice because the United States is blocking an oil pricing formula.
U.N. officials say Iraq faces a humanitarian emergency throughout the country because of a scarcity of food and medicine and inadequate water treatment because of sanctions.
